Add a per-App "working context" to the Nxeon admin board so a future Claude session (or the user) knows exactly where each app's code lives and how to build/deploy it. Then pre-fill the three existing apps, add an editor UI, and deploy to STAGING ONLY (do NOT promote to production). Work from /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma + Tailwind). The working tree is clean at commit 3e2f44e. Read relevant files before editing.

BACKGROUND: The board `App` model (prisma/schema.prisma) already has `{id, name, slug, color, serverId → Server, boards[]}`. The purpose of the boards is a Claude-facing, app-scoped work queue: board → App → Server (+ now: where the code is + how to deploy) so Claude can act on the right app. Server binding already gives SSH access (Server.ipAddress + platform-stored root password via `decryptSecret(server.rootPasswordEnc)`).

=== CHANGE 1: Schema ===
Add to `App`: `codePath String?`, `repoUrl String?`, `context String?` (context = free-form markdown: stack, build/deploy steps, conventions, gotchas). Apply with `npx prisma db push` against the prod `nxeon` DB (additive/nullable, safe).

=== CHANGE 2: Pre-populate the 3 existing apps (one-shot tsx script under scripts/, run then delete; async main(), no top-level await) ===
Set these ONLY where the field is currently empty/null (idempotent — never overwrite non-empty values a human may have edited). Match apps by slug.

App slug `nxeon`:
- codePath: `/opt/nxeon`
- repoUrl: derive at runtime via `git -C /opt/nxeon remote get-url origin` (if it errors, leave null)
- context (markdown):
"""
Nxeon platform — this admin app itself. Runs on the Proxmox host. Stack: Next.js (App Router) + Prisma + Tailwind. Code: /opt/nxeon. Prod: systemd `nxeon-web` (:80) + `nxeon-worker`. Staging: /opt/nxeon-staging, `nxeon-staging-web` (:8080). DB: Postgres "nxeon" (Prisma; uses `prisma db push`, NOT migrate). Deploy: commit (post-commit hook auto-pushes to GitHub main) → `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → `bash scripts/promote-production.sh`. Admin panel is served ONLY on the obscured host 4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud. NOTE: direct prod deploys via bash get safety-classifier-blocked — delegate deploys to a general-purpose subagent.
"""

App slug `soul-pilates`:
- codePath: `/opt/soulpilates`
- repoUrl: null (no repo on box — built images)
- context (markdown):
"""
Soul Pilates — LIVE studio-booking business (real customers — be careful). Server: studionexis-soul @ 51.79.226.200 (SSH via platform creds: decryptSecret(server.rootPasswordEnc)). Stack: .NET API + frontend, docker-compose. Code: /opt/soulpilates (docker-compose.prod.yml, compose project "soulpilates", env /opt/soulpilates/prod.env). Containers: soulpilates-prod-backend (.NET SoulPilates.API, host :8391→8080), -frontend (:3719), -mongo (db "soulpilates"), -redis, -rustfs (:6324), -glitchtip. Staging stack: /opt/soulpilates-staging (soulpilates-staging-*, frontend :3819, backend :8491). nginx on box: /etc/nginx/conf.d/00-soulpilates-com.conf + 01-soulpilates-staging.conf. Deploy: edit prod.env or rebuild image, then `cd /opt/soulpilates && docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml -p soulpilates --env-file prod.env up -d --force-recreate --no-deps <service>`. Email: sends via Nxeon Mail (mail.nxeon.cloud:587 as noreply@soulpilates.com.vn); templates are compiled into SoulPilates.Services.dll (not file-extractable). Mongo backups: /usr/local/bin/soulpilates-backup.sh (cron every 6h).
"""

App slug `studionexis`:
- codePath: `/opt/nexis`
- repoUrl: `https://github.com/santino1233/studionexis`
- context (markdown):
"""
Studio Nexis — Next.js studio-management app. Server: nexis-app @ 51.79.226.215 (SSH via platform creds). Repo: github.com/santino1233/studionexis. Code: /opt/nexis (prod) + /opt/nexis-staging (staging). Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router, Node 22, `next start -p 3105`, NOT standalone — copy the built .next), Prisma. Prod: systemd nexis-next.service (:3105). Staging: nexis-staging.service (:3106). DB: Postgres in the `nexis-postgres` container (bind 127.0.0.1:5599; DBs nexis + nexis_staging). Multi-tenant middleware: hq.studionexis.com = HQ portal, app./new. = admin hosts, HQ_PATH gates /hq, *.studionexis.com wildcard = tenants. Serves studionexis.com + www/hq/app/new/stg + tenant subdomains. Deploy: build .next + `systemctl restart nexis-next`. Wildcard cert /etc/letsencrypt/live/studionexis-wildcard/ (Cloudflare DNS-01 via /root/.cf-studionexis.ini). nginx: /etc/nginx/conf.d/studionexis.conf (nginx 1.24 → `listen 443 ssl http2`, not `http2 on`).
"""
Print which apps you updated and which fields were already set (skipped).

=== CHANGE 3: seed.ts ===
For fresh installs, add codePath/repoUrl/context defaults for the three known apps in prisma/seed.ts, but include them ONLY in the `create` clause — do NOT add them to the `update` clause (so a re-seed never overwrites human/Claude edits). Keep the existing name/color update behavior.

=== CHANGE 4: UI — app settings editor (components/admin/BoardClient.tsx + lib/actions-board.ts) ===
- Extend `AppSummary` + `listApps` to include codePath, repoUrl, context.
- Add an admin-gated server action `updateAppMeta(appId, { codePath?, repoUrl?, context? })` (revalidatePath("/admin/board")).
- Add an "App settings" affordance for the selected app (e.g. a small gear/edit button near the app header / next to the existing server picker) that opens a modal or panel to view+edit: color (optional), bound server (reuse existing setAppServer), **codePath** (text), **repoUrl** (text), **context** (a markdown textarea, decent height). Keep it cohesive with the dark theme; don't re-clutter the header — put the fields in a modal/drawer, not inline.
- Show a subtle indicator on the app (e.g. a tiny icon) when context is set, so it's discoverable. Preserve all existing board/app behavior.

=== AFTER EDITS ===
1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — zero errors in touched files.
2. `npm run build` — must compile.
3. `git add` ONLY changed files (schema.prisma, seed.ts, BoardClient.tsx, lib/actions-board.ts). NEVER `git add -A`; never stage `scripts/_*.ts` or secrets. Commit (message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`); post-commit hook auto-pushes — confirm via `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`.
4. Deploy to STAGING ONLY: `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh`; verify exit 0 + HTTP 200 on :8080.
5. **DO NOT run scripts/promote-production.sh.** Stop after staging.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT touch the Soul Pilates .200 box services, DNS, or mail config (reading Server rows from the nxeon DB via Prisma is fine).
- Do NOT `git add -A`. If a classifier blocks a command, report it verbatim and stop.

Return a structured report: schema change, which apps got which context fields pre-filled (and any skipped as already-set), seed.ts change, the editor UI added, typecheck/build status, commit hash + push confirmation, staging health, and explicit confirmation you did NOT deploy to production.

695	// ============================================================================
696	// SHARED HOSTING (Phase 1 foundation)
697	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
698	// A different product shape from VPS: many customers share ONE box, each with an
699	// isolated account (its own jailed Linux user + PHP-FPM pool + disk quota +
700	// name-based nginx vhost + scoped DB + mail). No per-customer VM.
701	//
702	// DNS model: every account on a HostingNode shares that node's SINGLE public IP.
703	// nginx routes by the Host header (name-based virtual hosting), so hundreds of
704	// domains live on one IP; the customer points an A record at `HostingNode.publicIp`
705	// (surfaced to them as the account's `pointTo`), and Let's Encrypt issues a
706	// per-domain cert served by SNI. These tables are additive — they do NOT touch
707	// the Server-scoped control panel (Website / VpsDatabase / AppInstall).
